newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty ceiling seen steady despite Wednesday gains.
newsitem.headline: Zloty ceiling seen steady despite Wednesday gains.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland allowed the zloty to strengthen past resistance at 1.5 percent from parity on Wednesday, but dealers said the central bank would probably force the local currency back down on Thursday.

"The NBP acted wisely because it knew that some banks had large amounts of dollars to sell on Wednesday and that this money was being constantly pushed out, making any intervention costly," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
"This does not mean the zloty's ceiling has been raised... and I would be surprised if on Thursday the NBP fixed the zloty at a similar level to today," Dryjski added.
Dealers said foreign capital inflows into Bank Handlowy's IPO amounted to at least $210 million and have kept the zloty buoyant this week.
"There was strong currency selling as banks lengthened positions on Wednesday, tested the central bank and because of other inflows," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty was fixed at 1.53 percent from parity, after two successive central bank fixes at 1.49 percent, both of which were lower than that day's market close.
On Wednesday the zloty closed at 1.58/1.53 percent from parity, stronger than Tuesday's 1.52/1.50 percent close.
Dealers said some foreigners sold T-bills in secondary trade on Wednesday to take advantage of the zloty's strength.

On the money market overnight and tomorrow/next rates both closed 0.10 point down to 21.60/21.80 and 21.65/21.85 percent respectively after the central bank refrained from staging any open market operations on Wednesday, dealers said.

The finance ministry will offer 1.3 billion zlotys worth of T-bills on Monday after it sold 382 million zlotys of 52-week bills on Wednesday. The average yield of these papers increased to 21.56 percent from the previous 21.49 percent.
